# Results — Study 319 (Lockup-Expiry) on the real tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Event basket from a hardcoded
table of recent US IPOs (listing dates from public exchange records); daily prices and the
SPY market benchmark from Yahoo! Finance adjusted closes via `yfinance`. Abnormal return =
stock daily return − SPY daily return (a market-adjusted synthetic control). The lock-up
expiry bar is set at the first close + 125 trading days (≈ 180 calendar days). As-of
**2026-06-18**.*

## Critical caveats

1. **Survivorship bias (named on the Signal axis).** The basket contains only tickers still
   queryable on yfinance. Of 32 listed IPOs, **29** had enough clean history around the
   expiry bar; `WORK` (Slack, acquired), `ZI`, `BIGC` failed to download. A current-membership
   basket can bias the sag in *either* direction — the worst post-expiry collapses may sit
   in names that delisted and dropped out.
2. **Anticipation.** The lock-up expiry date is disclosed in the S-1 and is **calendar-known
   months ahead**. Any rational sag should be at least partly front-run — so the cleanest
   read is an event study, not a calendar trade.
3. **Beta = 1 control.** We use a raw market-adjusted abnormal return (stock − SPY), not a
   fitted market-model alpha/beta. High-beta growth IPOs will carry residual market exposure;
   a per-event beta fit on short post-IPO histories is noisy, so we keep the simple control
   and flag it.
4. **Small n, mixed vintage.** 29 events spanning 2019–2024 across very different regimes
   (2021 SPAC mania → 2022 drawdown). Power is limited; pooling is a loose test.

## The expiry bar and the windows around it

| Window (tau) | n | Mean CAR | Median CAR | Sag-rate (CAR<0) | HAC *t* | 95% block-boot CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Expiry day only ([0,0] AAR) | 29 | **+62.9 bps** | — | — | **+0.87** | — |
| Run-up [−5,−1] | 29 | **−316.7 bps** | −391.6 | 62% | **−1.98** | [−645, +6] bps |
| Tight [−1,+1] | 29 | +74.2 bps | +35.5 | 45% | +0.56 | [−203, +350] |
| Post [0,+5] | 29 | **+322.7 bps** | +228.0 | 38% | +1.75 | [−93, +624] |
| Wide [−5,+5] | 29 | +6.0 bps | −193.2 | 55% | +0.02 | [−670, +547] |

**Finding.** There is **no significant abnormal sag at the lock-up expiry.** The expiry-bar
abnormal return is *positive* (+62.9 bps, *t* = +0.87) and the post-expiry window is
*positive too* (+322.7 bps, *t* = +1.75 — the wrong sign for the story). The single window
that leans the believers' way is the five-day **run-up** [−5,−1] (−316.7 bps, *t* = −1.98),
consistent with mild anticipation — but it does **not** clear |*t*| ≥ 2 and its bootstrap CI
touches zero. No window clears the inference bar with the predicted negative sign.

## The believers' trade made real

Shorting each IPO, market-hedged, over the post-expiry window [0,+5] (the window a "short the
unlock" trader would target):

| Cost (one-way, per leg) | Gross short PnL | Net short PnL | HAC *t* (net) | Win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps | **−322.7 bps** | −322.7 bps | −1.75 | 38% |
| 10 bps | −322.7 bps | −362.7 bps | −1.97 | 31% |
| 30 bps | −322.7 bps | −442.7 bps | −2.40 | 31% |

The short **loses money even gross** (the stocks tend to *rise* relative to the market just
after the unlock, the opposite of the folklore), and the loss only deepens once two legs of
one-way cost (stock + hedge, charged round-trip = 4× the one-way rate) are subtracted. The
run-up short [−5,−1] is the only profitable variant gross (+316.7 bps, *t* = +1.98) and it
decays below the bar after a single 10 bps cost on each leg.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** No event window around the lock-up expiry shows a significant negative
  abnormal return on this tape; the expiry-bar and post-expiry windows are positive, and the
  one negative window (the run-up) sits at *t* = −1.98, below the bar with a CI touching zero.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** The folklore short loses gross and worse net; the only positive
  variant (front-running the run-up) is wiped out by two-leg costs and would need short
  borrow on hard-to-borrow recent IPOs on top.
- **A predictable supply-shock sag? — Not supported.** Consistent with the modern literature
  (the lock-up effect documented by Field & Hanka 2001 and Bradley et al. 2001 has shrunk as
  the unlock became fully anticipated); on this 2019–2024 survivorship-biased basket there is
  no harvestable sag.

*The synthetic positive control (a planted −300 bps one-shot sag) is recovered cleanly by the
same engine — the harness can see a sag when one exists. It finds none on the real tape.*
